text:
anya: quick design sync 1: compact chart row feedback from usability session: axis labels get truncated and users can't tell whether numbers are tokens/sec or reqs/sec. also smoothing hides short-lived spikes people care about
peter: which page?
anya: Routes -> Throughput column in 3-col compact. sample: label shows 't.../sec' and tooltip just repeats 'throughput'. confusion in the session
tara: suggestion: use micro-unit abbreviations in-line (e.g., 'tok/s', 'req/s') and provide full unit in the tooltip: 'Tokens per second (tok/s)'. keeps row height stable and reduces truncation
oliver: smoothing note: default smoothing in compact mode is aggressive. customers missed 1-2s spikes. propose: smoothing off by default in compact; show a tiny toggle or hover smoothing for expanded view
peter: agree. also legend: when we collapse legend items, keep 1-line with an overflow chevron not to push chart down. ensure the chevron is keyboard-focusable
tara: accessibility: the unit needs an aria-describedby="p95-desc" where p95-desc reads 'P95 is the 95th percentile, typical of tail latency'
anya: copy nit: prefer 'P95 latency' over '95th' in most visible text. shorter '95th' is ambiguous to non-technical folks
oliver: outlier handling: render faint triangle glyphs visually but avoid per-point tooltips. surface a single summary control at the end of the sparkline: '3 spikes 30m ago7'. clicking opens a timeline panel with timestamps
peter: implementation: don't create DOM nodes for every marker in compact mode. draw markers in canvas / background-image and expose one button with the summary for screen readers
tara: analytics change: emit event sparkline_compact_summary_open with count and smoothing flag. also track whether users toggle smoothing in expanded view
design-bot: uploaded variant A (inline unit abbreviations + aggregate outlier control) and variant B (no abbreviations, wider unit column) to figma: https://figma.redwood/compact-axis/1823456780
anya: plan: oliver mocks aggregate control -> tara + peter run a11y pass (VoiceOver + NVDA) -> finalize copy -> ship behind prod-flag. estimate 1-2 dev days + design review
anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
